paragraphs: Mi shello yashan belel ereb rosh hashshana yakol leekol ad ammud hashshachar, abal mi sheyyashen lo yokal achar shena, veraq mashqeh shel qhvv" (qph) muttar qodem alot hashshachar:

clarification.explanation: One who did not sleep on the night of Erev Rosh Hashanah may eat until dawn. But one who has already slept should not eat after sleeping, and only drinking coffee is permitted to him before dawn.
takeaways: One who did not sleep: may eat until dawn
One who slept: may not eat after sleeping, and only coffee is permitted

paragraphs: En toqein beereb rosh hashshana lo bayyom velo ballayla apillu bebeto, veim hattoqea shel haqqahal rotzeh lehargil atzmo vetzarik hu lekak yitqa becheder sagur o bebor. veen nopelim al penehem beereb rosh hashshana, abal bemincha shellepanayv nopelim veomerim vidduy deha belel ereb rosh hashshana omerim vidduy uselichot venohagim lelek beereb rosh hashshana al haqqebarot velomar baqqashot sham, veal yasim megammato neged hammetim ella yitpallel lehashshem yitbarek sheyyitten lo rachamim bizkutam, veyakol lehishtatteach al qeber hatztzaddiq veyomar hareni mebaqqesh minnepesh hatztzaddiq haqqabur poh shettitpallel alay lipne hqb"h kak vekak, veyizzaharu bitpillat mincha shel ereb rosh hashshana ki hi tepilla haacharona (shel otah hashshana):

clarification.explanation: One does not blow the shofar on Erev Rosh Hashanah, neither by day nor by night, even at home; and the community's shofar-blower who needs to practice should do so in a closed room or in a pit. One does not recite Tachanun (falling on one's face) on Erev Rosh Hashanah itself, but at the Minchah of Erev Rosh Hashanah one does fall and recite Vidui, and likewise Vidui and Selichot are recited on the night of Erev Rosh Hashanah. It is customary to go to the cemetery on Erev Rosh Hashanah and recite supplications there; but one should not direct his intent to the dead themselves, rather pray to Hashem that He grant mercy in their merit, and one may ask the soul of a righteous person to pray for him before Hashem. One should be especially careful with the Minchah prayer of Erev Rosh Hashanah, since it is the last prayer of the year.
takeaways: The shofar is not blown on Erev Rosh Hashanah, and Tachanun is not recited during the day, but it is recited at the Minchah before it
At the cemetery one prays to Hashem in the merit of the righteous, not to the dead themselves

paragraphs: Mistapperin beereb rosh hashshana, vetob lehizzaher lehistapper qodem chatzot, ubeet shemmistapper yekavven lehaabir kochot haddinin, uleqayyem mitzvat happeot velobeshim lebanim berosh hashshana beemunatenu ubitchonenu bechasde hashshem yitbarak, vehu "p mah sheddareshu rabbotenu za"l bammidrash vekannizkar ballebush za"l, venohagin litbol beereb rosh hashshana mishshum qeri deepshar sheyyetze mimmennu ezeh tippa behishtanna velav addateh, vegam mishshum tuma detashmish hammitta, vegam kede leqabbel hearat qedushshat yom tob shel rosh hashshana lechayyim tobim uleshalom, laken tebila rishona yekavven bah bishbil tahora, usheniyya yekavven bah letiqqun hakkaas, ushelishit lematteq haddin vehaggebura bachasadim, urebiit lipshot mealayv bigde hachol, vikavven bazeh gam ken 'tikleh shana veqilloteha', vachamishit leqabbel alayv hearat qedushshat yom hazzikkaron vikavven bazeh 'tachel shana ubirkoteha' vegam hannashim yihyu zehirim litbol beereb rosh hashshana vaapillu habbetulot, utzerikin lisroq searot rosham techilla mishshum chatzitza, veken yibdequ gupam mishshear debarim hachotzetzin, veraq en tzerikin lehasir sear bet hashshechi ubet haerva veayyen bematteh eprayim:

Im haish anus shello yukal litbol, yishpok al gupo tisha qabbin mayim (beerek shettem esreh liter veshesh meot garam) bihyoto omed arom veyabo adam echad veyishpok alayv hammayim merosho vead raglayv, vetisha qabbin ellu hem kol qab hu tl"b drh"m, ki kol qab hu arbaa luggin vekol log hu q"ch drh"m vekannizkar bebet david dap ql"v, veim en lo keli echad sheyyakil kol tisha qabbin yechalleqem bishnayim o shalosh kelim abal yoter mishshelosha kelim en mitztarepin, veyizzaher lishpok hashsheni qodem siyyum qillucha harishon veken yaaseh bashshelishi, vekannizkar bammishna pereq g' demiqvaot veayyen shulchan aruk haggaon rabbenu zalman za"l siman tr"v umah shekkatab beture zahab siman p"ch hu taut soper, veim gam zeh eno yakol laasot tob sheyyittol yadayv arbaim peamim, vekak hasseder yaareh techilla al yad yamin paam achat vikavven beot rishona shel shem "b, veken paam achat al yad semol vikavven gam ken beot rishona shel shem "b, veod yaareh paam sheniyya al yamin vikavven beot sheniyya deshem "b, veken paam sheniyya al semol vikavven beot sheniyya veken al zeh hadderek ad asara peamim veyachazor viareh asara peamim bezeh achar zeh al yamin vikavven bekol paam beot achat daasara otiyyot shem "b viareh aach"k asara peamim bezeh achar zeh al semol vikavven bahem baasara otiyyot shem "b al hasseder nimtza sak hakkol arbaim peamim vekannizkar beseper "emet leyaaqob" ninayv za"l baqqunetres 'sepat emet' yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: One takes a haircut on Erev Rosh Hashanah, and it is good to take it before midday, intending to remove the forces of judgment and to fulfill the mitzvah of pe'ot. One wears white clothing on Rosh Hashanah out of faith and trust in the kindnesses of Hashem. It is customary to immerse on Erev Rosh Hashanah, out of concern for a drop of seminal emission, because of the impurity of marital relations, and in order to receive the holiness of the day; and one intends in the immersions: purity, rectifying anger, sweetening judgment, removing the weekday garments ("let the year and its curses end"), and receiving the holiness of the Day of Remembrance ("let the year and its blessings begin"). Women too, even unmarried maidens, should immerse, and should comb their hair and check their bodies for interposing matter (though there is no need to remove the hair of the armpits and pubic area). One who is prevented from immersing should pour nine kabbin of water (about 12.6 liters) over his body while standing naked, and another person should pour it over him from head to foot; it may be divided between two or three vessels (no more), provided the second is poured before the first stream ends. And if even this cannot be done, it is good to wash the hands forty times alternately (right and left), with the intentions of the letters of the Name of seventy-two.
takeaways: One takes a haircut, wears white, and immerses on Erev Rosh Hashanah (women and unmarried maidens as well)
One who cannot immerse: nine kabbin of water, or, if pressed, washing the hands forty times

paragraphs: Yihyeh ragil leekol berosh hashshana bishte hallelot al shulchano beseder zeh, techilla temarim vibarek 'bore peri haetz' veyokal temara achat, veaach"k yomar 'yehi ratzon sheyyittammu oyebenu' veku', veyokal temara hashsheniyya, vikavven bebaqqasha zo al oyebim hattachtonim, veaach"k yokal rvby" vehu mah sheqqorin bilshon arbe lvby" veyomar 'yehi ratzon sheyyirbu zekuyoteno', ulepi mah shekkatab haggaon magen abraham za"l sheyyebaqqesh gam lepi hammashmaut hannireh milleshon hammedina, al ken anachnu anshe bgd"d sheqqorin otah lvby" tzarik lomar 'sheyyirbu zekiyyoto utelabbebenu', vekaasher nohagim lomar biqra shette baqqashot 'shettiqra roa gezar dinenu' 'veyiqreu lepaneka zekiyyotenu' shehu mashmaut qeria al shem qr", veken hainyan brvby" lepi leshon medinatenu, veachar rvby" yokal kareti veyomar 'sheyyikretu oyebenu vesoneenu', vikavven bazeh al kochot haraot shennibreu mehaavonot shel adam uminnetzutze qeri asher alehem mekavvenim biqriat shema sheal hammitta vaalehem neemar "oyebe ish anshe beto", veachar kareti yokal saleqa veyomar 'sheyyistallequ oyebenu' veku' vikavven bazeh al hamqatregim vekochot haddin hammastinim lemala, veaach"k yokal "qara" veyomar 'shettiqra roa gezar dinenu' (vikavven beshem qr") 'veyiqreu lepaneka zekiyyotenu', veaach"k yokal rimmon matoq veyomar 'shennihyeh meleim mitzot karimmon', veaach"k yokal tappucha mebushshal besukkar veyomar 'yehi ratzon shettitchaddesh alenu shana toba umetuqaAdonai, veen omerim kidbash, vekatebu haacharonim za"l hattaam shemmebiin tappucha remez lachaqal tappuchin qaddishin besod "reeh recha beni kerecha sadeh", venireh li besiyyata dishmayya taam lattappucha belel rosh hashshana ki hattappucha yesh bo shelosha hanaot taam umareh verecha, vehu lesiman tob lebaqqashatenu shepa hakkelali shehu 'bene chayye mezone' lekol hashshana kullah, veod nireh li besiyyata dishmayya taam acher "p mah shekkatab bazzohar haqqadosh parashat shemini dap m' bappasuq "rappeduni betappuchim", tappucha appeq chamra umekavven reuta dela yazziq chamra, vehaynu deokelin tappucha achar yayin kede shello yazziq lahem hayyayin, velaken minhag bene adam latet tappucha letok kos hayyayin ukemo shekkatub basseparim, veyadua shehayyayin hem geburot venimtza hattappucha hu mebassem haggeburot, veatta berosh hashshana kol miggammatenu hu lebassem ulematteq haggeburot lekak okelin tappucha, veod nireh li bs"d taam acher, deita bazzohar haqqadosh kol happerot sharesham bammalkut veraq hattappucha sharesho bedukra shehu sod tiperet ukemo shekkatabti haqdama zo bemaqom acher, veyadua mah shekkatab rabbenu haari"y za"l dechadeshe haqqayitz hem benuqba shehi sod hammalkut minnisan vead tishre, vechadeshe hachorep mittishre vead nisan hem bedukra shehi sod hattiperet, velaken belel rosh hashshana shehu hatchalat chadeshe haddukra okelin tappucha sheshsharesho bedukra:

Veachar hattappucha nohagin leekol rosh kebes, umebaqqeshim 'yehi ratzon shennihyeh lerosh velo lezanab' 'vetizkor lanu aqedato veillu shel yitzchaq abinu ben abraham abinu alehem hashshalom', veim lo haya yakol lehabi rosh kebes lo yabi rosh shel z ki hu 'dina qashya' kannizkar bazzohar haqqadosh parashat shemini dap m" ammud b' veayyen od bazzohar chadash seder toledot, velaken tob shello yegaddel adam z betok beto ulepachot yizzaher bazeh berosh hashshana ushear aseret yeme hatteshuba shello yimtza bebeto oz, veal ken lo yabi lepanayv berosh hashshana rosh z deim lo nimtza lo rosh kebes yabi shel op, vetzarik sheyyabiu mebushshal ulekak yinqob rosh haggulgolet shello veyimlachennu vibashshelennu, verosh op zakar hu yoter tob merosh op neqeba lesimana taba, ukeshemmebi rosh op lo yomar bebaqqasha ella raq 'shennihyeh lerosh velo lezanab', abal en omerim 'vetizkor lanu aqedato veillu shel yitzchaq abinu' ella berosh kebes, veyesh osin seder hannizkar leel bemaakalim hannizkarim leel gam beyom rosh hashshana beshacharit vekannizkar b'matteh eprayim', veken anachnu nohagim bebetenu lehabi kol hannizkar leel al hashshulchan gam bayyom:

clarification.explanation: One should be accustomed to hold, on both nights of Rosh Hashanah, an order of omen-foods (simanim) at his table: first dates, with the blessing "Borei Peri Ha'etz" and eating a date, then saying "May it be Your will that our enemies be finished" and eating a second date. Then rubia (lubia), saying "that our merits increase and win our hearts"; karti (leek), "that our enemies be cut off"; silka (beet), "that our enemies be removed" (regarding the accusers); kara (gourd), "that the harshness of our verdict be torn and our merits be read before You"; a sweet pomegranate, "that we be filled with mitzvot like a pomegranate"; and an apple cooked in sugar, "that a good and sweet year be renewed upon us" (and one does not say "like honey"). The later authorities wrote that eating the apple alludes to the "holy field of apples" - a holy field mentioned in the secret of the Zohar - based on the verse "See, the scent of my son is like the scent of the field." And our teacher [the Ben Ish Chai] added further reasons of his own for eating the apple, among them: that it has three pleasures (taste, appearance, and smell) as a sign of general abundance of children, life, and sustenance; that the apple sweetens the severities (as an apple is placed in wine); and that its root is in the aspect of "the male" (Tiferet), with which the winter months begin. After the apple, one eats the head of a sheep - bringing it cooked: piercing the skull, salting, and cooking it - and requests "that we be as a head and not as a tail" and "remember for us the binding of Isaac." One should not bring the head of a goat, which represents harsh judgment (and it is good not to raise a goat at home, especially during the Ten Days of Repentance); and if there is no head of a sheep, one brings the head of a fowl (male preferred), saying regarding it only "that we be as a head and not as a tail." Some hold this order also on the day of Rosh Hashanah at Shacharit, and so did [the Ben Ish Chai] practice.
takeaways: The order of omen-foods on both nights: date, rubia, karti, silka, kara, pomegranate, apple, sheep's head

The apple is eaten for several reasons: a kabbalistic allusion to the "holy field of apples" in the Zohar, its three pleasures (taste, appearance, and smell), the sweetening of the severities, and its root in the attribute of Tiferet
One does not bring the head of a goat (harsh judgment); in the absence of a sheep's head one brings the head of a fowl

paragraphs: Lo yoklu berosh hashshana debar chimmutz velo tabshil mebushshal bedabar chimmutz, veken yizzaharu mipperot chamutzim hen rimmonim hen anabim hen aggasim, vekatab b'matteh eprayim' dehu haddin shello yokal peri shello nigmar adayin bishshulo, uminhag tob leekol basar shamen umine metiqa lesimana taba ak lo yarbeh bahem lemallovt kereso ella 'toameha chayyim zaku', veyishteh shetiyyot arebot al pi hakkatub beezra "iklu mashmannim ushetu mamtaqqim veshilchu manot leen nakon lo ki qadosh hayyom laadonenu veal teatzebu ki chedvat Adonai hi mauzzekem", depasuq zeh neemar al yom rosh hashshana kayyadua:

clarification.explanation: One does not eat anything sour on Rosh Hashanah, nor a dish cooked with something sour, and one should be careful of sour fruits (pomegranates, grapes, sour pears), and likewise of a fruit that has not finished ripening. It is a good custom to eat fatty meat and sweet foods as a good omen, but one should not indulge to the point of filling his stomach, for "its tasters merit life"; and one should drink pleasant drinks, based on the verse in Ezra, "Eat the fat and drink the sweet... for the joy of Hashem is your strength," which is said regarding Rosh Hashanah.
takeaways: One does not eat sour food, sour fruits, or fruit that has not finished ripening
One eats fatty meat and sweets as a good omen, but in moderation, not to excess

paragraphs: Yizzaher shello yikos, demillebad chomer issur hakkaas shehu qasheh bekol zeman, hinneh hu beyom rosh hashshana eno siman tob laadam, vehaishsha tzerika lihyot zeriza laarok hashshulchan ulekassoto bemappa yapa qodem sheyyabo balah mibbet hakkeneset kede shebbeboo yimtza hashshulchan aruk vehu lesiman tob, im im nizdammen shebba velo raa hashshulchan aruk lo yitqotet im ishto veyikas dehakkaas hu siman ra beyoter, ella yisbol velo yaqpid apillu balleb:

clarification.explanation: One should be careful not to become angry, for besides the gravity of the prohibition of anger at all times, on Rosh Hashanah it is not a good omen. The wife should be diligent to set the table and cover it with a fine cloth before her husband comes from the synagogue, so the table will be found set - a good omen. And if it happens that he comes and does not find the table set, he should not quarrel with his wife or become angry, for anger is an especially bad omen; rather he should bear it and not be resentful even in his heart.
takeaways: Care about not becoming angry is especially great on Rosh Hashanah, since it is not a good omen
The wife sets the table before the husband's arrival, and the husband should not be resentful even in his heart

paragraphs: Qodem qiddush yesheb bemoshabo al mitta mutztzaat veyomar petichat eliyyahu zakur lattob ad 'qum rabbi shimon veyitchaddeshun' veku', aach"k yomar pasuq (bereshit v, ch) "venoach matza chen beene Adonai" shettem esreh peamim, veaach"k pasuq (sham kv, yb) "vayyizra yitzchaq baaretz hahi" veku' shettem esreh peamim, veaach"k pasuq (tehillim lo, y) "ki immeka meqor chayyim beoreka nireh or" asara peamim, veaach"k pasuq (sham kv, yb) "or zarua latztzaddiq uleyishre leb simcha" shiba asar peamim veaach"k (shemuel  kh, v)"vaamartem koh lechay veatta shalom ubeteka shalom" veku' asara peamim, veyomar 'tachel shana ubirkoteha' veyaamod leqaddesh:

clarification.explanation: Before Kiddush he sits on a made bed and recites "Petichat Eliyahu" until "Kum Rabbi Shimon." Afterward he says the verse "And Noah found favor in the eyes of Hashem" twelve times, "And Isaac sowed in that land" twelve times, "For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light do we see light" ten times, "Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright of heart" seventeen times, and "So may you live, and peace be to you, and peace to your house" ten times, and says "Let the year and its blessings begin" and stands to recite Kiddush.
takeaways: Before Kiddush one recites "Petichat Eliyahu" and verses a set number of times
One concludes with "Let the year and its blessings begin" and stands to recite Kiddush

paragraphs: Beqiddush bishte hallelot yebarek 'shehecheyanu', veim nizdammen lo peri chadash yannichennu lepanayv al hashshulchan belel sheni keshemmebarek 'shehecheyanu' vikavven alayv, ak en tzarik lehaqpid lachazor al dabar zeh, vekol seder lel ' yaaseh belel b', veyilmod al hashshulchan bishte hallelot mishna masseket rosh hashshana vikavven keneged shem dn"y, ak yizzaher lilmod otah binima, venohagin lilmod gam leshon zohar haqqadosh hannidpas bammachazorim:

clarification.explanation: At the Kiddush of both nights, one blesses "Shehecheyanu." If he has a new fruit, he should place it before him on the second night at the time of the "Shehecheyanu" blessing and intend upon it, though there is no need to insist on this. The whole order of the first night is done on the second night as well, and one studies at the table on both nights a Mishnah from Tractate Rosh Hashanah (with a pleasant melody, with intent toward the Name Adonai), and it is customary to study also the language of the Zohar printed in the Machzorim.
takeaways: One blesses "Shehecheyanu" on both nights; on the second night a new fruit is good (but not essential)
One studies a Mishnah from Tractate Rosh Hashanah and the language of the Zohar on both nights

paragraphs: Im chal tebilat mitzva belel rosh hashshana yeshammesh veyitbol babboqer, vehammitchassed lidchot hattashmish shel tebilat mitzva hare zeh chasidut shel shetut vaapillu im enah tebila shel mitzva im roeh shennitorera taavato harbeh al ishto yeshammesh veyitbol babboqer kede shello yabo chas vechalila lide tumat qeri, vekol inash yada benapsheh:

clarification.explanation: If the night of the mitzvah immersion (the wife's night of immersion) falls on the night of Rosh Hashanah, he should have relations and immerse in the morning, and one who is stringent to postpone relations connected with the mitzvah immersion - this is a foolish piety. And even if it is not a mitzvah immersion, if he sees that his desire has become greatly aroused, he should have relations and immerse in the morning, so as not to come to the impurity of seminal emission; and every person knows himself.
takeaways: A mitzvah immersion falling on the night of Rosh Hashanah: he has relations and immerses in the morning; postponing this is a foolish piety
If his desire is greatly aroused, he should have relations to prevent seminal emission

paragraphs: Shene yamim shel rosh hashshana qedushsha achat hen, ubetza shennoleda bazeh asura bazeh, veken hannitztzod o nitlash bazeh asur bazeh, veim rosh hashshana chal beyom chamishi veshishshi asur gam beshabbat sheacharehem, vesapeq nolad beereb rosh hashshana sapeq beyom rosh hashshana hare zeh asur:

clarification.explanation: The two days of Rosh Hashanah have one continuous holiness, and therefore an egg laid on the first day is forbidden also on the second, and likewise something trapped or plucked on this day is forbidden on the second day. And if Rosh Hashanah falls on Thursday and Friday, the prohibition continues also to the Shabbat that follows them. And if it is doubtful whether the thing came into being on Erev Rosh Hashanah or on Rosh Hashanah itself, it is forbidden.
takeaways: The two days of Rosh Hashanah are one continuous holiness: what is born or trapped on one day is forbidden on the other
If they fall on Thursday and Friday, the egg is forbidden even on the following Shabbat; a doubtful case is forbidden

paragraphs: En yeshenim beyom rosh hashshana, vetzarik lehizzaher sheyyitorer mishshinto ballayla qodem alot hashshachar, veim yesh lo keeb harosh o shear mechosh shemmukrach lishon bayyom, yitappeq veyashen achar chatzot hayyom:

clarification.explanation: One does not sleep during the daytime of Rosh Hashanah, and one must take care to wake up at night before dawn. And one who has a headache or another ailment that forces him to sleep during the day should restrain himself and sleep only after midday.
takeaways: One does not sleep during the day on Rosh Hashanah, and one wakes before dawn
One who must sleep because of an ailment should wait until after midday

paragraphs: Seder hattashlik osin apillu chal rosh hashshana beshabbat veken nimtza katub biktibat yad harab mvhr"y antebbi za"l beshem rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, veim neenas velo asa hattashlik beyom rishon, yaaseh bayyom hashsheni achar musap, ken matzati katub beseper 'tora lishmah' ketibat yad:

clarification.explanation: One performs the order of Tashlich even when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat, as Rabbi Yehuda Antebi wrote in the name of the Rashash. And one who was prevented and did not perform Tashlich on the first day should perform it on the second day after the Musaf prayer, as [the Ben Ish Chai] found written in the book Torah LiShmah.
takeaways: Tashlich is performed even on Shabbat
One who was prevented and did not perform it on the first day performs it on the second day after Musaf

paragraphs: Berosh hashshana en omerim 'machul uselach laaonotenu', utzerikin lehizzaher bebaqqasha sheomerim qodem tehillim veachar tehillim ledalleg leshonot ellu, v"g dekatab bazzohar haqqadosh asur lepirsha chataayv behay yoma, haynu davqa beqol ram abal belachash beet teqiat shopar dimyushshab kesheshshoheh hattoqea ben tshr"t ltsh"t uben tsh"t ltr"t yitvaddeh belachash al chataayv bipratut, ubesiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l mesuddar nosach vidduy lehitvaddot ben hassedarim hannizkarim:

clarification.explanation: On Rosh Hashanah one does not say "Pardon and forgive our sins," and one must be careful to skip these expressions in the supplications recited before and after Tehillim. And although the Zohar writes that it is forbidden to specify one's sins on this day, this means specifically aloud; but in a whisper, during the "Meyushav" [seated] shofar blowings, when the blower pauses between the sets of blasts (Tashrat, Tashat, Tarat), one may confess his sins in detail in a whisper, and in the Siddur of the Rashash a text of confession is arranged for between the sets.
takeaways: One does not say "Pardon and forgive" on Rosh Hashanah; these expressions are skipped
It is permitted to confess in a whisper (not aloud) between the sets of the seated shofar blowings

paragraphs: Yomar beperush qodem sheyyitqa 'hareni mukan bitqiot ellu shel meyushshab veshel haamida bekullam lehotzi kol hashshomea yede chobato', d"p shehu mukan lekak missetama, tob leparesh bepiv, uben hattoqea uben hatztzibbur lo yasichu ben teqiot dimyushshab litqiot dimummad, vehappesuqim upiyyut shennohagim hatztzibbur leomeram qodem tepillat musap achar chazarat seper tora lahekol lo yomrem hattoqea:

clarification.explanation: Before the blowings he should state explicitly: "I am hereby prepared, with these blowings, both of the seated and of the standing [sets], to fulfill the obligation of all who hear" - even though he is presumably prepared for this anyway, it is good to state it explicitly. The blower and the congregation should not converse between the blowings of the "seated" set and those of the "standing" set. The verses and the liturgical poem that the congregation customarily recites before Musaf (after the return of the Torah scroll) should not be recited by the blower.
takeaways: The blower declares aloud that he intends to fulfill the obligation for the listeners
One does not converse between the seated and standing blowings; the blower does not recite the poem before Musaf

paragraphs: Yekasseh hashshopar ad gemar habberakot, vetzarik sheyyochazennu beyado beet habberaka mekusseh veayyen 'rosh mashbir' siman l', veqodem habberaka yakkeh beyado al habbima kede sheyyargishu kol hatztzibbur shehu mukan lebarek veyittenu datam al habberaka, veyomar 'birshut mori verabbotay' vibarek beqol ram vikavven lehotzi hatztzibbur yede chobatam, veim yesh adam yosheb rachoq min hattoqea vechush hashma shello chalush devadday eno shomea habberakot heteb az yebarek leatzmo keshemmebarek hattoqea veyishma hatteqiot, veyesh meqomot nohagim laamod beet habberaka shel teqiat shopar veyesh meqomot shello nahagu laamod, upoh irenu lo nahagu laamod:

clarification.explanation: The blower keeps the shofar covered until the blessings are finished, and holds it in his hand covered during the blessing (see Rosh Mashbir). Before the blessing he strikes his hand on the bimah, so that the whole congregation will sense that he is ready to bless and pay attention, and he says "By the permission of my teachers and masters," and blesses aloud, intending to fulfill the obligation for the congregation. And if there is a person sitting far from the blower whose hearing is weak, so that he certainly does not hear the blessings well, he should bless for himself while the blower blesses, and listen to the blowings. In some places it is customary to stand at the blessing of the shofar blowing, and in some it is not; and in our city it was not customary to stand.
takeaways: The blower holds the shofar covered during the blessing, strikes the bimah so people will pay attention, says "By the permission of my teachers and masters," and blesses aloud to fulfill the obligation for the congregation.
One who sits far away with weak hearing should bless for himself and [then] listen to the blowings.
Some are accustomed to stand at the blessing and some are not (and in his city they did not stand).

paragraphs: Yochaz hashshopar beyad yamin umaamido gam ken betzad yamin im epshar lo, vegam teqia rishona yomar lo hammiqra, veyizzaher shello yihyeh hashshopar pagum bimqom hannachat peh apillu pegima kol dehu, vitaqqenu qodem rosh hashshana:

clarification.explanation: He should hold the shofar in his right hand and position it to the right side if possible, and even for the first blowing the caller should call out [the sequence] to him. He must be careful that the shofar not be blemished at all at the place where the mouth is placed, even a slight blemish, and it should be fixed before Rosh Hashanah.
takeaways: He holds the shofar in his right hand and to the right side; even for the first blowing the caller calls out the sequence to him
The shofar must not be blemished at the place where the mouth is placed; it is fixed before Rosh Hashanah

paragraphs: Mi shenneenas velo ba lebet hakkeneset uba hattoqea lebeto litqoa lo shelosh peamim tshr"t veshalosh peamim tsh"t veshalosh peamim tr"t tzarik zeh laamod beet hatteqiot, ki ellu hem etzlo chiyyub shel tora vetzarik lihyot meummad duvmya dispirat haomer, yaan ki hu eno shomea teqiot beseder tepillat musap ubeellu yotze y"ch middeorayta, vehannashim peturot min haddin ki zo mitzvat aseh shehazzeman geramah, ak rob hannashim qabeu mitzva zo alehem betorat chiyyub ubaim lebet hakkeneset lishmoa qol shopar, velaken haishsha shennahaga bekak kamma shanim naaseh aliyya chiyyub, veim neensa shello hayeta yekola labo lebet hakkeneset yabo hattoqea etzlah lebetah veyitqa lah ak lo tebarek veken nahagu bebetenu, veishsha shennahaga bemitzva zo venizdammen lah paam achat shello tukal labo lebet hakkeneset vegam lo tukal lehabi toqea lebetah taaseh hattora beereb rosh hashshana al qabbalat hamminhag:

clarification.explanation: One who was prevented and did not come to the synagogue, and the blower comes to his home to blow for him three times Tashrat, three Tashat, and three Tarat, must stand during the blowings, since for him these constitute a Biblical obligation (like the counting of the Omer), because he does not hear the blowings in the order of Musaf, and through these he fulfills his Biblical obligation. Women are exempt from this obligation (a positive, time-bound commandment), but most women have accepted this mitzvah upon themselves as an obligation and come to hear the shofar, and therefore a woman who has been accustomed to do so for several years, it becomes an obligation for her; and if she was prevented, the blower should come to her home and blow for her without a blessing. And if she cannot even bring a blower, she should perform, on Erev Rosh Hashanah, an annulment of her acceptance of the custom.
takeaways: One who is prevented and hears the blowings at home stands, since for him they are a Biblical obligation
A woman who has been accustomed to the mitzvah becomes obligated in it; if prevented, she hears it at home without a blessing, or performs an annulment

paragraphs: Min rosh hashshana ad yom hakkippurim omerim 'hammelek haqqadosh', veim amar 'hael haqqadosh' o shehu mesuppaq chozer lerosh hattepilla, veim amar 'hael haqqadosh' vetekep nizkar vesiyyem 'hammelek haqqadosh' vekak hayeta amirato 'hael haqqadosh hammelek haqqadosh' yatza, veim hashlicha tzibbur taa bachazara gam ken chozer larosh vechozer veomer qedushsha, veken bibraka 'meen sheba' name haddin ken v"p sheyyesh choleqin bibraka 'meen sheba' la amerinan 'sapeq berakot lehaqel' neged sebarat rabbenu haari"y za"l desabar beraka 'meen sheba' hi bimqom chazara ukemo shekkatabti besassipri haqqadosh 'mqbtzyl':

clarification.explanation: From Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur one says "HaMelech HaKadosh." If one said "HaEl HaKadosh," or is in doubt, he returns to the beginning of the prayer. And if he said "HaEl HaKadosh" and immediately remembered and concluded "HaMelech HaKadosh" (so that he said "HaEl HaKadosh HaMelech HaKadosh") he has fulfilled his obligation. Likewise, if the cantor erred in the repetition he returns to the beginning and recites the Kedushah again, and the same applies to the blessing "Me'ein Sheva" (of Friday night). And although there are those who differ regarding "Me'ein Sheva," one does not say "when in doubt about blessings, be lenient" against the opinion of the Ari, that this blessing stands in place of the repetition.
takeaways: During the Ten Days of Repentance: "HaMelech HaKadosh"; one who erred or is in doubt returns to the beginning of the prayer
One who corrected himself immediately after "HaEl HaKadosh" has fulfilled his obligation; a cantor who erred returns and repeats the Kedushah

paragraphs: Bebirkat 'hashibaAdonai omer 'hammelek hammishpat', veim taa veamar 'melek oheb tzedaqa umishpat' kevan dezakar 'melek' eno chozer, v"g demera"n sebira lehu chozer qayma lan 'sapeq berakot lehaqel' apillu keneged sebarat mera"n za"l ukemo shekkatabti bsh"q 'mqbtzyl':

clarification.explanation: In the blessing "Hashivah Shofteinu" [Restore our judges], one says, during the Ten Days of Repentance, "HaMelech HaMishpat." And if he erred and said "Melech Ohev Tzedakah U'Mishpat," since he mentioned "Melech," he does not return. And although Maran holds that he should return, we follow "when in doubt about blessings, be lenient," even against his opinion.
takeaways: In the blessing "Hashivah": "HaMelech HaMishpat"
If he erred and said "Melech Ohev Tzedakah U'Mishpat," he does not return, since he mentioned "Melech"

paragraphs: Im siyyem habberaka velo amar 'zekarenu' u'me kamoka' eno chozer, vaapillu amar "baruk atta Adonai" venizkar eno rashshay lesayyem 'lammedeni chuqqeka' kede lomar 'zakerenu' u'me kamoka', veita beseper 'tora lishmah' d'zakerenu' kevan shehi baqqashat rachamim im lo amarah bimqomah yomar otah b'shomea tepillaAdonai ubeshabbat uberosh hashshana yomar otah qodem sheyyaaqor raglayv, mah sheen ken 'mi kamoka' en lah tashlumin deenah baqqashat rachamim, veken baamirat 'vekatub' veku' 'ubeseper' veku' deim shakach eno chozer, ak yomar otah qodem sheyyaaqor raglayv dehem baqqashat rachamim:

clarification.explanation: If he concluded the blessing without saying "Zochreinu" or "Mi Chamocha," he does not return, and even if he said "Baruch Atah Hashem" and then remembered, he may not conclude "Lamdeni Chukecha" [instead] in order to say them. According to Torah LiShmah, "Zochreinu," being a request for mercy, if forgotten in its place, should be said in "Shome'a Tefillah" (and on Shabbat and Rosh Hashanah, before withdrawing his feet [at the end of the Amidah]); but "Mi Chamocha" has no makeup, since it is not a request for mercy. Likewise "V'chetov" and "U'vesefer," if forgotten, he does not return, but should say them before withdrawing his feet, since they are requests for mercy.
takeaways: One who forgot "Zochreinu"/"Mi Chamocha" and concluded the blessing does not return
"Zochreinu," "V'chetov," and "U'vesefer" (requests for mercy) can be made up; "Mi Chamocha" cannot

paragraphs: Bemusap shel rosh hashshana veshabbat shuba veyom hakkippurim yomru 'mi kamoka ab harachamim', veken hu haddin bemincha shel shabbat shuba, vegam im chalu rosh hashshana veyom hakkippurim beshabbat yomar bemincha 'ab harachamim', ukesheomer bemusap rosh hashshana pasuq "Adonai tzebaot yagen alehem", yaaseh tenua shel sop pasuq ki zehu pasuq bizkarya vesiyyumo zeh, abal mah sheomer achare zeh 'Adonai tzebaot yagen alekem' veku' zehu baqqasha, ukesheomer "veattem haddebeqim" veku' kesheyyaggia leot t' shel "tiktebenu" yedalleg tebat "hayyom" deen lehachziq atzmo ketzaddiq gamur shenniktabim berosh hashshana vekannizkar b'lebush' za"l, veyizzaher lomar 'tiktebenu berachameka lechayyim tobim' bishbil harashi tebot shello tihyeh tl"t, veken beot p"h yomar 'hayyom tipqedenu berachameka lechayyim tobim':

clarification.explanation: In the Musaf of Rosh Hashanah, Shabbat Shuvah, and Yom Kippur one says "Mi Chamocha Av HaRachamim," and likewise at Minchah of Shabbat Shuvah, and even if Rosh Hashanah or Yom Kippur falls on Shabbat, one says "Av HaRachamim" at Minchah. In the Musaf of Rosh Hashanah, when saying "Hashem Tzeva'ot yagen aleihem," one uses the cantillation for the end of a verse (since this is a verse in Zechariah), but the following "Hashem Tzeva'ot yagen aleichem" is a request. And in "V'atem hadeveikim," upon reaching the letter tav of "tichtevenu," one skips the word "hayom" [today], so as not to consider oneself a completely righteous person immediately inscribed on Rosh Hashanah, and says "tichtevenu berachamecha lechayim tovim" (for the sake of the acrostic); and at the letter peh, one says "hayom tifkedeinu berachamecha lechayim tovim" - specifically including the word "today," unlike at the letter tav.
takeaways: One says "Mi Chamocha Av HaRachamim" at Musaf and at Shabbat Shuvah

In "V'atem hadeveikim": at the letter tav one skips "today" and says "tichtevenu berachamecha lechayim tovim"; at the letter peh one says "hayom tifkedeinu berachamecha lechayim tovim" - with the word "today"

paragraphs: Kesheomer 'zakerenu lechayyim' yekavven lehamshik chayyim lanneshama, ukesheomer 'ketabenu beseper chayyim' yekavven lehamshik chayyim laggup, vikavven rosh 'zekarenu' z' vehassop m', mispar hvy"h hy"h shehem chakema ubina, ukesheomer 'zoker yetzurayv berachamim lechayyim' yekavven zeh al hanneshamot shezzoker otam berachamayv lehachaziram lechayyim lehachayotam baolam hazzeh besod chazaratam begilgul umizzeh yitammet etzlenu inyan techiyyat hammetim, ukesheomer 'hayyom harat olam im kebanim im kaabadim', katab rabbenu harasha"sh za"l kesheomer ken kol atzmotayv yochazemo rd leki yipqod hqb"h: 'im ab ani ayyeh kebodi veim adonim ani ayyeh morai', velaken yomar zeh bemittun veshibron leb, velaken hamminhag sheggam bachazara omerim zeh betzibbur beqol ram millebad hashlicha tzibbur:

clarification.explanation: Among the intentions in the prayer: when saying "Zochreinu LeChayim," one intends to draw life to the soul, and when saying "Kotveinu BeSefer Chayim," to draw life to the body. "Zocher Yetzurav BeRachamim LeChayim" is directed at the souls that Hashem returns to life in the secret of reincarnation, from which the matter of the resurrection of the dead is confirmed for us. "HaYom Harat Olam, im keVanim im ka'Avadim" should be said slowly and with a broken heart, so that all one's bones tremble as he says: if as sons, where is His honor, and if as servants, where is His awe; and therefore the custom is to say it also in the repetition, aloud, by the congregation (in addition to the cantor).
takeaways: The intentions of "Zochreinu"/"Kotveinu": life for the soul and for the body; "Zocher Yetzurav" alludes to the resurrection of the dead
"HaYom Harat Olam" is said slowly and with a broken heart, also in the repetition, aloud

paragraphs: Benussach yehi ratzon shel tehillim katub 'venizkeh venichyeh shibim shana veim bigburot shemonim shanaAdonai veek yomar ken hazzaqen sheshshinnayv yoter mishshemonim veod apillu shello higgia adayin leshibim lamma yishal dabar qatzub veshemma hqb"h natan lo chayyim yoter, al ken lo yomar zeh hannussach, ella yomar kak 'venizkeh lechayyim arukkim tobim umetuqqanim' ubenussach zeh vadday yesh sod shebbo mebarekim kohen gadol bemotzae kippur betzeto leshalom min haqqodesh:

clarification.explanation: In the text of the "Yehi Ratzon" recited after Tehillim it is written "that we merit and live seventy years, and if with strength, eighty years" - but how can an elderly person who has already passed eighty say this? And furthermore, why should a person ask for a fixed measure, when perhaps Hashem will give him more? Therefore one should not say this text, but should say "that we merit long, good, and proper years," and this text contains a secret, for with it the High Priest is blessed at the conclusion of Yom Kippur as he emerges in peace from the Holy place.
takeaways: One does not say "seventy years... eighty years" (a fixed number)
One says "that we merit long, good, and proper years"

paragraphs: Baaseret yeme teshuba en osin hapsaqa shel taanit deen nakon lehitannot ballayla gam ken, mippene shebbeyamim ellu iqqar hattiqqun naaseh "y akila ushetiyya, velule sheanachnu mukrachim lehitannot bayyom baabur tiqqun aonotenu lo hayinu mitannim gam bayyom, veatta sheanachnu mitannim bayyom anachnu somekim lehashlim hattiqqun "y akila ushetiyya shebballayla, velaken katub beseper 'tora lishmah' shetztzarik leekol pat bekol layla baaseret yeme teshuba kede lebarek 'birkat hammazon':

clarification.explanation: During the Ten Days of Repentance one does not observe a "hafsakah" fast (one continuing into the night), since it is not proper to fast at night during these days, because in these days the essential rectification is achieved specifically through eating and drinking; and were we not compelled to fast during the day for the rectification of our sins, we would not fast at all, and therefore we complete the rectification through the eating and drinking of the night. Therefore Torah LiShmah writes that one should eat bread every night during the Ten Days of Repentance in order to recite Birkat HaMazon.
takeaways: One does not fast at night during the Ten Days of Repentance, since the rectification is achieved through eating and drinking
One eats bread every night in order to recite Birkat HaMazon

paragraphs: Kalla shehi ubalah somekim al shulchan chamiha vachamotah, ulekak bekol hashshana kullah chamotah totzi challa min haissa utebarek, hinneh baaseret yeme teshuba tishtaddel liqqach hakkalla maot mibbalah vetaqqana bo qemach shiur challa, kede shetteqayyem hi beatzmah haprashat chala bibraka lepachot paam achat beshana:

clarification.explanation: A young married woman who, along with her husband, relies on the table of her father-in-law and mother-in-law - and throughout the year the mother-in-law separates challah and blesses - during the Ten Days of Repentance should make an effort to take money from her husband and buy with it flour in the measure of challah, so that she herself may fulfill the mitzvah of separating challah with a blessing, at least once a year.
takeaways: A young wife who relies on her mother-in-law's table should separate challah herself during the Ten Days of Repentance
In order to fulfill the mitzvah with a blessing at least once a year
